Let's remind ourselves of the special trigonometric ratios, as given by the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253746/assets/d93c490adbb5cdbc0e9a09b60eea9b82ab93be8e871e334423abc17ddd62955e.png)

- Let's first consider the angle $150^\circ.$ From the unit circle, we see that the angle $150^\circ$ corresponds to the point 

$$
\left( -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2} \right).
$$

 Since the sine of the angle corresponds to the $y$-coordinate, we have 

$$
\sin 150^\circ  = \dfrac{1}{2}.
$$

- Now, let's consider the angle $240^\circ.$ From the unit circle, we see that the angle $240^\circ$ corresponds to the point 

$$
\left( -\dfrac{1}{2}, -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \right).
$$

 Since the sine of the angle corresponds to the $y$-coordinate, we have 

$$
\sin 240^\circ  = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Using the fact that $\csc{\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡{240}^{∘} & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{240}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we combine the results:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡({150}^{∘})+2{csc}^{2}⁡({240}^{∘}) & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+2{(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+2(\frac{4}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{8}{3} \\  & =\frac{35}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
